CVE-2026-35616 exploitation attempt against edge SOHO/IoT devices — JDY initial access AIExploitation Medium
JDY operators weaponise newly disclosed edge-device vulnerabilities for initial access, with CVE-2026-35616 named explicitly in the article. Hunts vendor advisories and edge-device telemetry for exploit attempts targeting devices from the named vendor list (Cisco RV320/RV325, Araknis, Mimosa, Ubiquiti, Draytek, Hikvision, Linksys). Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-35616 as the JDY operators' delivery vector for the shell-script dropper. Combined with Black Lotus Labs' named-vendor list (Cisco RV320/RV325, Araknis, Mimosa, Ubiquiti, Draytek, Hikvision, Linksys) the asset filter is high-precision. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/china-linked-jdy-botnet-expands-to-1500.html • https://blog.lumen.com/black-lotus-labs/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vuln scanner probing the same CVE on internal edge devices
  • Pen-tester sanctioned engagement against the same vendor lab
  • Vendor management traffic accessing /cgi-bin/ admin endpoints legitimately
  • Misclassified internal management traffic from a NOC subnet
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (lookup_table("sanctioned_scanners"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: confirm targeted device is actually one of the named vendor/model classes (Cisco RV320/RV325, Araknis, Mimosa, Ubiquiti, DrayTek, Hikvision, Linksys) and check firmware against the CVE-2026-35616 advisory. Step 2 — contain: if exploit attempt succeeded (HTTP 200 + subsequent outbound shell-script-style request), isolate the device, dump config, and rotate any shared credentials. Step 3 — hunt: pivot the attacker's source IP across 30 days of perimeter logs — JDY scanner bots probe before exploitation, so the same IP often shows wide-fanout TCP/SSL fingerprinting first.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-35616"
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where DeviceCategory in ("NetworkDevice","IoT") or Vendor in~ ("Cisco","Araknis","Mimosa","Ubiquiti","DrayTek","Hikvision","Linksys")) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, OSPlatform, Vendor, Model, IsInternetFacing
| order by IsInternetFacing desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ ("Cisco","Fortinet","PaloAlto","Snort","Suricata")
| where Message has "CVE-2026-35616" or DeviceEventClassID has "35616" or RequestURL has_any ("/cgi-bin/","/setup.cgi")
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == true
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, Message, Activity
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(cisco.asa OR paloalto OR fortinet OR snort OR suricata) ("CVE-2026-35616" OR @url:(*\/cgi-bin\/* OR *\/setup.cgi*))

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer

status: experimental

            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities

The Hacker News
2026-06-10 11 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Fortinet, Ivanti, and SAP have released security updates to address multiple critical security vulnerabilities that could result in arbitrary code execution and information disclosure. The security flaw patched by Fortinet relates to a command injection vulnerability in FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS WEB UI. It's tracked as CVE-2026-25089 (CVSS score: 9.1). Ivanti Sentry command injection via /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage (CVE-2026-10520) AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated HTTP POSTs to the Ivanti Sentry (MobileIron Sentry) MICS endpoint exploited by CVE-2026-10520, where attacker-controlled MICS configuration commands are dispatched to the handleExecute() backend for root RCE. The endpoint path is uniquely associated with this CVE and should be a high-fidelity exploit primitive. Rationale: Endpoint path /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage and backend function handleExecute() are explicitly named in the article quoting watchTowr Labs' write-up — both are unique to CVE-2026-10520 and not in any benign baseline. Excluding 401/403/302 strips the post-patch redirects Ivanti added. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/product-alerts • https://labs.watchtowr.com/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the path
  • Penetration-testing engagements coordinated with IT
  • Ivanti TAC engineers running diagnostic POSTs during a support case
  • Security-research lab Sentry instances mirroring production traffic
  • Internal red-team CVE replay exercises
Suppression filter
| where SrcIp !in (dynamic(["<scanner-cidrs>","<redteam-jump-host>"])) and UA !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","InsightVM")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full HTTP request body, source IP, and User-Agent. Confirm the Sentry version is below R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1 — if it is patched, the request still indicates reconnaissance. Check whether 200/500 was returned vs the post-patch 302 to /login. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF/edge, isolate the Sentry appliance from production MDM traffic, and snapshot disk + memory for forensics. Rotate any MobileIron Sentry admin credentials and API tokens. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the source IP across all internet-facing assets, hunt for child shells spawned by the Sentry tomcat process, audit /tmp and /var/log on the appliance for staged tooling, and verify no new admin accounts were created (link to CVE-2026-10523 UC).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","HttpConnectionInspected")
| where RemoteUrl has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
   or AdditionalFields has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let suspect_path = "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has suspect_path
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, SrcIp=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=strcat(csUriStem,iif(isnotempty(csUriQuery),strcat("?",csUriQuery),"")), Status=scStatus, UA=csUserAgent),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has suspect_path or Message has suspect_path
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="WAF", Computer=DeviceName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UA=RequestClientApplication),
    (AzureDiagnostics
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where Category in ("ApplicationGatewayAccessLog","FrontdoorAccessLog","ApplicationGatewayFirewallLog")
        | where tostring(Properties) has suspect_path or ResultDescription has suspect_path
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AzureWAF", Computer=Resource, SrcIp=tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).clientIp), Method=tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).httpMethod), Uri=tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).requestUri), Status=tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).httpStatus), UA=tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).userAgent)))
| where Status !in ("401","403","302")
| summarize Hits=count(), Methods=make_set(Method,5), Statuses=make_set(Status,5), Uris=make_set(Uri,5), UAs=make_set(UA,5) by bin(TimeGenerated,1h), Computer, SrcIp, Source
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry unauthenticated admin account creation (CVE-2026-10523) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of new administrative accounts on Ivanti Sentry without a preceding authenticated session — the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-10523, an authentication-bypass that lets unauthenticated attackers mint full admin credentials. Pivots on Sentry audit log shipped via syslog plus Defender/Sentinel logon telemetry for the new credentials being reused inward. Rationale: CVE-2026-10523 explicitly lets an unauthenticated attacker mint admin accounts on Sentry — so the high-fidelity signal is an admin-add audit line with no authenticated actor field, anchored to the Sentry/MobileIron product. The Defender join finds the newly-minted account then being used inside the estate. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/product-alerts
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bootstrap of a new Sentry node where the installer creates the initial admin
  • Ivanti professional services rebuilding a Sentry instance during DR test
  • Configuration management (Ansible/Puppet) provisioning a service admin
  • Sentry HA failover writing role-assign events from the system context
  • Legitimate password-recovery flows that recreate a locked admin
Suppression filter
| where NewUser !in (dynamic(["admin","installer","setup"])) and not (HostName has "sentry-dr" and dayofweek(TimeGenerated) in (0d,6d))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the Sentry audit log around the admin-add and confirm there's no authenticated session ID or operator user preceding it; correlate with the watchTowr CVE-2026-10520 endpoint UC for chained exploitation. Step 2 (contain): Disable the new admin account on Sentry, force-rotate ALL Sentry local admin credentials, terminate active web sessions, and block external access until patched to R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1. Step 3 (hunt): Search SigninLogs and DeviceLogonEvents for the new username across the estate (MDM enrolment changes, mailbox rule changes, VPN logins). Audit MDM policy changes pushed since the account was created — attackers will use Sentry admin to retarget managed devices.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain, LogonType, RemoteIP, RemoteDeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SentryAdminVerbs = dynamic(["adduser","createuser","createadmin","user.add","admin.create","role.assign","AddLocalAdmin"]);
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HostName has_any ("sentry","mobileiron") or ProcessName has_any ("mics","sentry","tomcat")
| where SyslogMessage has_any (SentryAdminVerbs) or SyslogMessage has_cs "role=admin" or SyslogMessage has "administrator"
| extend NewUser = extract(@"(?i)user(?:name)?[=:\s]+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend Actor = extract(@"(?i)by[=:\s]+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)

| project TimeGenerated, HostName, ProcessName, NewUser, Actor, SyslogMessage
| join kind=leftouter (
    SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | project SignInTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName
) on $left.NewUser == $right.UserPrincipalName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fortinet FortiSandbox WEB UI command injection HTTP pattern (CVE-2026-25089) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiSandbox / FortiSandbox Cloud / FortiSandbox PaaS WEB UI containing OS-command metacharacters in parameters — the CVE-2026-25089 CWE-78 vector. FortiSandbox WEB UIs are not internet-routine HTTP endpoints, so reduction by shell-metacharacter content gives a high-signal sweep. Rationale: Article explicitly cites CWE-78 (OS command injection) via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' to FortiSandbox WEB UI — so the detection anchors on the FortiSandbox host context AND classic shell-metacharacter payloads (URL-encoded newlines, command substitution, pipe-to-shell). Combining the target host filter with the injection regex avoids most generic noise. Cross-checked against: • https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised security scanners with shell-metacharacter test payloads (Nessus, Burp scans)
  • Penetration testers fuzzing the FortiSandbox WEB UI
  • Legitimate API consumers that URL-encode special characters in filenames being submitted for sandbox analysis
  • FortiSandbox internal cluster sync traffic that includes encoded payloads
  • Defender for Cloud Apps reverse-proxy injecting encoded query strings
Suppression filter
| where Src !in (dynamic(["<scanner-cidrs>"])) and UA !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Burp","sqlmap")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full request URL, body, source IP, and response code. Confirm FortiSandbox version against the affected list (5.0.0-5.0.5, 4.4.0-4.4.8); if patched (5.0.6+/4.4.9+) treat as recon. Look for response codes 200/500 versus 400/403. Step 2 (contain): Block source IP at the perimeter, isolate FortiSandbox management plane from internet, snapshot config and audit logs. If FortiSandbox PaaS/Cloud, open a Fortinet TAC case immediately. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on source IP across all Fortinet appliances; on the FortiSandbox itself, hunt for unexpected child processes of the WEB UI service, new cron jobs, and modifications under /data or /var. Verify no sandbox-analysis results were tampered with to hide other malware verdicts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","HttpConnectionInspected")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("fortisandbox","/cgi-bin/fsa","FortiSandbox")
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("fortisandbox","FortiSandbox")
| extend Url = tolower(strcat(tostring(RemoteUrl)," ",tostring(AdditionalFields)))
| where Url matches regex @"(%0a|%0d|%26%26|%7c%7c|%24%28|%60|;\s*(id|whoami|uname|wget|curl|cat\s+/etc)|\|\s*(id|whoami|sh|bash|nc)|`[^`]+`|\$\([^)]+\))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let injection_re = @"(?i)(%0a|%0d|%26%26|%7c%7c|%24%28|%60|;\s*(id|whoami|uname|wget|curl|cat\s+/etc)|\|\s*(id|whoami|sh|bash|nc)|`[^`]+`|\$\([^)]+\))";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where DeviceProduct has_any ("FortiSandbox","FortiGate","FortiWeb") or DestinationHostName has "sandbox" or RequestURL has_any ("fortisandbox","/cgi-bin/fsa")
        | extend Composite = strcat(tostring(RequestURL)," ",tostring(Message))
        | where Composite matches regex injection_re
        | project TimeGenerated, Src=SourceIP, Dst=DestinationIP, Host=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, UA=RequestClientApplication, Msg=Message),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where sSiteName has_any ("sandbox","fortisandbox") or csUriStem has_any ("/cgi-bin/fsa","/fortisandbox/")
        | extend Composite = strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery)
        | where Composite matches regex injection_re
        | project TimeGenerated, Src=cIP, Dst=Computer, Host=sSiteName, Method=csMethod, Url=Composite, UA=csUserAgent, Msg=""))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SAP NetWeaver SAML XML signature wrapping anomaly (CVE-2026-44748) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts SAML SSO authentications to SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP where the asserted identity differs from the signed assertion's original subject — the operational signature of XML signature wrapping (XSW) against the SAP SAML verifier per CVE-2026-44748. Correlates SAP-side audit logon with the IdP's emitted subject to spot identity mismatch. Rationale: Article and Onapsis quote describe XSW: 'modified signed XML documents with tampered identity information' accepted by the verifier. The detection key is identity mismatch — SAP-side audit shows a user/IP for which the IdP has no matching successful SAML issuance, or shows it from a different source IP. The SAP audit-log codes (AUW=successful logon, AU1=logon) and SAML AssertionConsumer pivot anchor it to NetWeaver AS ABAP. Cross-checked against: • https://onapsis.com/blog • https://support.sap.com/en/my-support/knowledge-base/security-notes-news.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1606.002 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IdP log ingestion lag exceeding the 30-minute window
  • User changed source IP between IdP sign-in and SAP assertion consumption (mobile→VPN handoff)
  • Test SAP tenants using federation with a non-monitored IdP
  • Service accounts (SAPSYS/DDIC/SOLMAN) doing SAML on behalf of background jobs
  • Multiple IdPs federated to SAP where one isn't shipped to Sentinel
Suppression filter
| where SapUser !in (dynamic(["SAPSYS","DDIC","SOLMAN_ADMIN","SOLMAN_BTC"])) and SapUser !startswith "SVC_"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Extract the full SAP audit record and matching SAML AuthnRequest/Response from the SP. Decode the assertion (xmlsec1 verify) and confirm whether the Subject NameID matches the SignedInfo reference. Validate SAP NetWeaver kernel/SAP_BASIS patch level against SAP Security Note for CVE-2026-44748. Step 2 (contain): Force-terminate the SAP session, revoke the affected SAP user's auth tickets, and lock the SAP account pending review. If validated, take the NetWeaver SAML SP into maintenance and restrict access to IdP source ranges only. Step 3 (hunt): Search SAP audit for all logons by that user in the last 30 days for similar IP/IdP mismatch, audit changes to SAP_ALL/SAP_NEW role grants, review transactions SU01/SE38/SE16 for sensitive table access during the suspicious window.
let SAP_SAML = AlertEvidence
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where AdditionalFields has_any ("SAP NetWeaver","SAML","ABAP")
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, RemoteIP, AdditionalFields;
let IdpSAML = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where AuthenticationRequirement has "singleFactor" or AuthenticationDetails has "SAML" or ResourceDisplayName has_any ("SAP","NetWeaver","ABAP")
    | summarize IdpHits=count(), LastIdpSignin=max(Timestamp) by AccountUpn, IPAddress, ResourceDisplayName;
SAP_SAML
| join kind=leftouter IdpSAML on AccountUpn
| where isnull(IdpHits) or IdpHits == 0 or RemoteIP != IPAddress
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, SAPSourceIP=RemoteIP, IdpSourceIP=IPAddress, IdpHits, ResourceDisplayName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 7d;
let SapSamlLogons = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("sapstartsrv","disp+work","icman","saposcol") or HostName has_any ("sap","abap","netweaver")
    | where SyslogMessage has "SAML" and (SyslogMessage has_any ("AUW","AU1","logon successful") or SyslogMessage has "AssertionConsumer")
    | extend SapUser = extract(@"(?i)(?:user|usr|subject)[=:\s]+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | extend SapSrcIp = extract(@"(?i)(?:from|src|ip)[=:\s]+(\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(SapUser)
    | project SapTime=TimeGenerated, HostName, SapUser, SapSrcIp, SyslogMessage;
let IdpSamlIssues = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ResourceDisplayName has_any ("SAP","NetWeaver","ABAP","Fiori") or AppDisplayName has_any ("SAP","NetWeaver")
    | where ResultType == 0
    | project IdpTime=TimeGenerated, IdpUpn=tolower(UserPrincipalName), IdpUser=tostring(split(UserPrincipalName,"@")[0]), IdpSrcIp=IPAddress, AppDisplayName;
SapSamlLogons
| extend SapUserLc = tolower(SapUser)
| join kind=leftouter IdpSamlIssues on $left.SapUserLc == $right.IdpUser
| where isempty(IdpUpn)
    or (isnotempty(IdpSrcIp) and isnotempty(SapSrcIp) and IdpSrcIp != SapSrcIp)
    or datetime_diff('minute', SapTime, IdpTime) > 30 or datetime_diff('minute', SapTime, IdpTime) < -5
| project SapTime, HostName, SapUser, SapSrcIp, IdpTime, IdpUpn, IdpSrcIp, AppDisplayName
| order by SapTime desc
(source:sap OR source:syslog) AND (@host:(*sap* OR *netweaver* OR *abap*) OR @process.name:(sapstartsrv OR disp+work OR icman)) AND (@message:*SAML* AND (@message:*AssertionConsumer* OR @message:*"logon successful"* OR @message:AUW OR @message:AU1)) AND NOT @usr.name:(SAPSYS OR DDIC OR SOLMAN_* OR svc-*)

Unpatched Ivanti Sentry / FortiSandbox / SAP NetWeaver in software inventory AIWeaponization High
Flags hosts in Defender TVM (or Sentinel DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities) running versions still vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089, CVE-2026-10520, CVE-2026-10523, CVE-2026-44748, CVE-2026-27671, CVE-2026-22732, or CVE-2026-40128 — giving the SOC a prioritized fix list while the patch advisory is fresh. Rationale: Article enumerates concrete vulnerable version ranges (FortiSandbox 5.0.0-5.0.5 / 4.4.0-4.4.8; Sentry below R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1; specific SAP NetWeaver/Commerce Cloud/Data Hub builds) plus seven CVE IDs — perfect input for a Defender TVM CVE list query. Internet-facing flag prioritizes Ivanti Sentry and FortiSandbox edge devices. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/product-alerts • https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt • https://support.sap.com/en/my-support/knowledge-base/security-notes-news.html
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM signature lag where a patched host hasn't re-reported software inventory yet
  • Standby/cold appliances brought online for DR test
  • Out-of-support evaluation lab instances
  • Vendor-managed appliances (FortiSandbox PaaS/Cloud) where Microsoft TVM has no visibility — these won't appear and need vendor portal check
  • Recently rebuilt host pulling old image
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Export the device list with internet-facing flag and machine group. Confirm SoftwareVersion against the article's exact ranges, deduplicate against your CMDB owner-of-record, and identify any FortiSandbox PaaS/Cloud tenancies that need Fortinet portal validation (not Defender-visible). Step 2 (contain): For internet-facing instances, restrict management plane access by source IP allow-list while patching, and coordinate emergency change windows with the application owners. For SAP, schedule the SAP_BASIS kernel patch via SUM/SPAM. Step 3 (hunt): For each affected device, run the per-CVE exploitation UCs (this article's UC1 for the Sentry endpoint, UC3 for FortiSandbox WEB UI, UC4 for SAP SAML) over the last 30 days to confirm none were pre-emptively exploited before the patch lands.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Endpoint exposure to CISA KEV adds: Chrome V8, Cisco SD-WAN Manager, Arista EOS (June 2026) AIWeaponization High
Inventory-driven exposure check for the three CVEs CISA added to KEV on 2026-06-10: CVE-2026-11645 (Chrome V8 OOB R/W, CVSS 8.8), CVE-2026-20245 (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager command injection, CVSS 7.8), and CVE-2026-7473 (Arista EOS tunnel decapsulation, CVSS 6.9, no patch planned). FCEB agencies must remediate by 2026-06-23 per BOD 22-01; this UC surfaces which managed devices still carry the vulnerable software so triage can prioritise patch or mitigation. Rationale: Hard-coded to the three CVE IDs CISA explicitly added in this article (CVE-2026-11645/20245/7473). TVM tables return one row per (device, CVE) with the patched-version reference, so this is high-fidelity, near-zero-FP exposure tracking against the KEV deadline of 2026-06-23 named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Device decommissioned but still reporting from cached agent telemetry
  • CVE flagged on Chrome 'beta channel' build that ships behind stable
  • Air-gapped or isolated network segments where exposure exists but exploitation is not feasible
  • TVM stale signature data hours behind actual patch deployment
  • Arista 7020R/7280R/7500R appliances not configured as tunnel endpoints (per article, exploitation requires VXLAN VTEP / GRE / decap-group config) but still flagged on version match
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVendor in~ ("Google","Cisco Systems","Cisco","Arista Networks","Arista")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on each row's Hosts list; for Chrome rows confirm browser version via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory; for Arista rows check whether the device is actually configured as a tunnel endpoint (VXLAN VTEP, GRE, decap-group) — only those are exploitable. 2) Contain: push Chrome patch via management tool; for Cisco SD-WAN Manager apply vendor-fixed image; for Arista EOS apply the upstream/local ACL mitigation Arista published (no patch is planned). 3) Hunt: for any host that was unpatched during the public-PoC window, run the companion UC 'Chrome browser spawning LOLBin children post-V8 exploit' over the same time range to verify no exploitation occurred.

Chrome browser spawning LOLBin children post-V8 sandbox-escape (CVE-2026-11645) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for chrome.exe spawning command interpreters or living-off-the-land binaries — the canonical post-exploitation footprint after a V8 RCE escapes the renderer sandbox. CVE-2026-11645 is described in the article as a V8 OOB R/W achieving code execution 'inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page', so the in-the-wild kill chain requires an additional sandbox escape; that escape almost always manifests as the browser process tree growing a non-Chrome child. Rationale: Pivots on the article-specific claim that CVE-2026-11645 is a V8 OOB R/W giving 'arbitrary code execution inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page' — meaning a successful in-the-wild kill chain must escape the renderer sandbox, which manifests as chrome.exe parenting non-Chrome processes. The Defender query joins to DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory so the analyst sees the Chrome version alongside the suspicious spawn — devices that are unpatched AND showing this pattern jump to the top of the queue.
ATT&CKT1203 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise SSO / smartcard helpers that invoke certutil.exe from chrome.exe
  • 'Open in PowerShell' / 'Open in Terminal' from a webmail attachment context menu
  • Browser-launched MSI/EXE installers spawning a cmd /c wrapper during install
  • Chromium DevTools 'Run command' shelling to a sysadmin's preferred CLI
  • Custom enterprise browser extensions that exec helper binaries (e.g. Citrix Receiver launchers)
Suppression filter
| where not(FileName =~ "certutil.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sso","smartcard","-user")) and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("chrome_proxy.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","chrome_pwa_launcher.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the device's Chrome version from DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory and check it against the CVE-2026-11645 patched build. If the version is patched, the alert is almost certainly an extension/SSO false positive — close. 2) Contain: if Chrome is unpatched and the child is cmd/powershell with discovery commands (whoami, net, nltest, systeminfo) or download primitives (certutil, bitsadmin, curl), isolate the device, kill the chrome.exe tree, and collect the child process command line + SHA256 for IR. 3) Hunt: for the same device, pivot DeviceNetworkEvents on InitiatingProcessFileName == 'chrome.exe' for the last 24h to find the lure URL/IP, then sweep the org for other users who hit the same URL with an unpatched build.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--type=renderer","--type=utility","--type=gpu-process")
   or isempty(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","tasklist.exe","systeminfo.exe","qwinsta.exe","reg.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory | where SoftwareName has "Chrome" | summarize ChromeVersion = any(SoftwareVersion) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ChromeVersion, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildBinary = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\chrome.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\nltest.exe","\\tasklist.exe","\\systeminfo.exe","\\qwinsta.exe","\\reg.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Chrome Browser Spawning LOLBin Child Post V8 Sandbox Escape (CVE-2026-11645)
id: 7d5a3c8e-9b2f-4e1a-bb7c-2f1e6d4a8c3d
description: Detects google chrome.exe spawning command interpreters or LOLBins, the canonical post-exploitation tell of a renderer sandbox escape. Tuned for hunting CVE-2026-11645 V8 out-of-bounds R/W exploitation in the wild after CISA added it to KEV on 2026-06-10.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Web-facing exposure of dev.env / .env config file (returns 200) · [LLM] github.com/dhax/go-base supply-chain footprint in go.mod / build artifacts · [LLM] Internal host clones / curls github.com/dhax/go-base or raw dev.env · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Admin / privileged API call without a preceding SUCCESSFUL login (JWT forgery indicator) · [LLM] JWT token in HTTP Authorization header verifying against secret 'random'
Web-facing exposure of dev.env / .env config file (returns 200) AIReconnaissance High
Hunts HTTP requests to dev.env / .env / .env.* paths that returned a 2xx response, indicating a misconfigured web server is leaking the very file that ships AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random. CVE-2026-48031 weaponises exactly this file, so any successful retrieval is a direct precursor to JWT forgery. Rationale: Targets the exact filename (dev.env) named at line 10 of the advisory plus common .env variants the same template is renamed to. 2xx/3xx status confirms the leak actually happened. Cross-checked CVE-2026-48031 advisory and dhax/go-base PR #31. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal CI/CD pipeline pulling .env from a private artifact server
  • DAST/SAST scanners (Burp, ZAP, Nessus) probing for exposed dotfiles
  • Penetration testers running ffuf / dirsearch with default wordlists
  • Internal developer documentation site serving a sanitized .env.example
  • Cloud config-management agents (Consul, etcd) syncing env templates over HTTP
Suppression filter
and csUserAgent !has_any ("Burp","OWASP ZAP","Nessus","Qualys","Nuclei","ffuf","dirsearch","gobuster") and cIP !in (KnownScannerIPs)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on cIP/sourceIPAddress; was the request from a known scanner, a developer subnet, or external? Inspect User-Agent and response size — non-empty 200 on dev.env is critical. 2) Contain: rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET immediately to a 32+ byte random value, invalidate all outstanding JWT/refresh tokens, and add a WebACL/NGINX deny for .env/dev.env paths. Take the affected service off the perimeter if the secret was leaked externally. 3) Hunt: look for forged-token use — admin API calls from the same source IP within 24h, /api/v1/token/refresh hits with unknown sub claims, and any new sessions whose iat predates the secret rotation. Sweep all Go services for github.com/dhax/go-base in go.mod.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/dev.env","/.env","/.env.dev","/.env.local","/.env.development")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe","devenv.exe","goland64.exe","idea64.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
// IIS-fronted Go service exposure
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(dev\.env|\.env(\.[a-z]+)?)$"
| where scStatus in (200,206,301,302)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceProduct in ("WAF","Application Gateway","CloudFront","NGINX","Apache")
    | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(dev\.env|\.env(\.[a-z]+)?)(\?|$)"
    | where toint(EventOutcome) between (200 .. 399)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, sSiteName=DestinationHostName, cIP=SourceIP, csMethod=RequestMethod, csUriStem=RequestURL, csUriQuery="", scStatus=toint(EventOutcome), csUserAgent=RequestClientApplication
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

github.com/dhax/go-base supply-chain footprint in go.mod / build artifacts AIReconnaissance High
Identifies hosts (developer laptops, CI runners, container build agents) where go.mod, go.sum, vendor/modules.txt or Dockerfiles reference github.com/dhax/go-base. The advisory states 'all versions before commit cc82b974...' are vulnerable, so footprinting the dependency is the first step before patching can begin. Rationale: Anchors on the exact module path github.com/dhax/go-base named in the advisory's Affected Component list. go.mod / go.sum / Dockerfile additions and `go build`/`go mod` invocations that reference the module pin the asset surface that needs patching to the cc82b974... commit. Cross-checked CVE-2026-48031 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/commits/master
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer evaluating the boilerplate for a new microservice
  • Security team running SCA scan that already covers this CVE
  • CI job intentionally pinning to the patched commit (>= cc82b9740fa6)
  • Internal fork of go-base that is already patched
  • Vulnerability scanner (Trivy, Grype, Snyk) reading go.sum files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trivy.exe","grype.exe","snyk.exe","syft.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: list every host/build agent that touched go.mod referencing dhax/go-base in the last 30d. For each, pull the pinned version (the @ pseudo-version after the path). Anything before commit cc82b9740fa6 (2026-05-17) is vulnerable. 2) Contain: file Jira/Linear tickets to bump the dependency past cc82b9740fa6, regenerate AUTH_JWT_SECRET (>=32 chars), and force a token revocation on next deploy. Block new builds on the unpatched version via a renovate/dependabot policy. 3) Hunt: identify all running services derived from the vulnerable code — query container registries for images whose go.mod includes the unpatched pin. For any that were ever internet-facing, run the JWT-forgery UC against their access logs back to the deploy date.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("go.mod","go.sum","modules.txt","Dockerfile")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| union (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCmdline", FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("go.mod","go.sum","modules.txt","Dockerfile")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| union (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath=ActingProcessName, TargetFileName=ActingProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Admin / privileged API call without a preceding SUCCESSFUL login (JWT forgery indicator) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Forged tokens signed with the hardcoded 'random' secret never traverse the application's login or refresh flows — they appear as bearer-auth-only requests. This UC pivots web access logs for /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/me hits whose source IP has no /api/v1/login/* 2xx in the prior 24h, the behavioural signature of token forgery. Rationale: The advisory's PoC explicitly hits /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, and /api/v1/token/refresh with a forged Bearer token (no login step). Modelling 'admin hit without a recent successful login from same IP' captures that footprint without requiring the JWT to be parsed. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Long-lived legitimate session whose original login was >24h ago (refresh token kept it alive)
  • Service-to-service auth using a static API key rather than the login flow
  • Healthcheck / synthetic monitoring hitting /api/v1/me with a pre-baked token
  • CI smoke tests that obtain tokens out of band and never use /login
  • NAT'd corporate egress where many users share one source IP and not all have logged in
Suppression filter
and csUserName !in ("healthcheck","synthetics","datadog","newrelic") and csUserAgent !has_any ("Pingdom","StatusCake","Datadog Synthetics","kube-probe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the JWT from the Authorization header — decode header+payload (no signature check needed) and verify the 'sub' and 'roles' claims match a real user. Compare 'iat' against the user's last legitimate login from your IdP. 2) Contain: if the token is forged, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ byte random value, restart the Go service, and force-revoke all sessions. Block the source IP at the WAF. 3) Hunt: pull all requests from the same IP and from the same user-agent over the prior 30 days. Look for /api/v1/admin/users enumeration, mass /api/v1/me lookups across different sub claims (token re-use across identities), and any state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE that may have already exfiltrated data.
let AdminHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl;
let LoginHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(48h)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/login/","/api/v1/auth/")
    | summarize LastLogin = max(Timestamp) by RemoteIP;
AdminHits
| join kind=leftouter LoginHits on RemoteIP
| where isnull(LastLogin) or datetime_diff('hour', Timestamp, LastLogin) > 24
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LastLogin, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let AdminHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/api/v1/(admin/|me$|token/refresh)"
    | where scStatus < 400
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUriStem, csUserAgent, csUserName;
let LoginHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(48h)
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/api/v1/(login|auth)"
    | where scStatus < 400
    | summarize LastLogin = max(TimeGenerated) by cIP;
AdminHits
| join kind=leftouter LoginHits on cIP
| where isnull(LastLogin) or datetime_diff('hour', TimeGenerated, LastLogin) > 24
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUriStem, csUserAgent, csUserName, LastLogin
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:caddy) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/admin/* OR */api/v1/me OR */api/v1/token/refresh) @http.status_code:[200 TO 299] @http.request_headers.authorization:Bearer*
# log group: /aws/applicationelb/access-logs  (ALB access logs — adjust per ELB)
fields @timestamp, request_url, client_ip, elb_status_code, user_agent
| filter request_url like /(?i)\/api\/v1\/(admin\/|me$|token\/refresh)/
      and elb_status_code >= 200
      and elb_status_code < 400
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.user) as users values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/admin/*","*/api/v1/me","*/api/v1/token/refresh") Web.status IN (200,201,204) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=outer src [ search index=web (url="*/api/v1/login/*" OR url="*/api/v1/auth/*") status<400 earliest=-24h | stats max(_time) as login_time by src ] | where isnull(login_time) OR login_time < (firstTime - 86400) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.user) as users values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/admin/*","*/api/v1/me","*/api/v1/token/refresh") Web.status IN (200,201,204) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=outer src [ search index=web (url="*/api/v1/login/*" OR url="*/api/v1/auth/*") status<400 earliest=-24h | stats max(_time) as login_time by src ] | where isnull(login_time) OR login_time < (firstTime - 86400) | sort - lastTime
Internal host clones / curls github.com/dhax/go-base or raw dev.env AIReconnaissance Medium
Catches developer or attacker hosts pulling the vulnerable boilerplate — either via 'git clone github.com/dhax/go-base', 'go get', or direct curl/wget of raw.githubusercontent.com/dhax/go-base/.../dev.env. Either action seeds the secret 'random' onto a system that may later run the service or be used to forge tokens. Rationale: Hits the exact module path github.com/dhax/go-base from the advisory's Affected Component plus the raw.githubusercontent.com pattern used when an attacker just wants the leaked dev.env without cloning. Narrowing to git/go/curl/wget keeps the volume sane. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base
ATT&CKT1593.003 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer learning Go and trying the popular boilerplate (1,685 stars on GitHub)
  • Security researcher pulling the repo to reproduce the CVE
  • CI mirror sync that mirrors many public Go modules including go-base
  • Internal training material that references go-base as an example
  • Dependency-resolution side-effect when a transitive module points back here
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("renovate","dependabot","snyk.exe","trivy.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: validate the host — is it a dev workstation, a build agent, or a production server? Production server is the worst case. Capture the destination path of the clone to know where the secret 'random' now lives on disk. 2) Contain: if production, rip out the deployed artifact and rebuild from a patched commit (>= cc82b9740fa6). On dev hosts, ensure the dev.env file is not later copied into a release container. 3) Hunt: from the same host/user, look for subsequent 'go build' artifacts being pushed to internal registries, container image pushes labelled with the developer's name, and any web service deployed from those artifacts now serving /api/v1/* on the network.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","go.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)raw\.githubusercontent\.com/dhax/go-base/[^\s]+dev\.env"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(git|go|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh)(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)raw\.githubusercontent\.com/dhax/go-base/[^\s]+dev\.env"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Clone / fetch of github.com/dhax/go-base (CVE-2026-48031)

JWT token in HTTP Authorization header verifying against secret 'random' AIActions on Objectives High
Decodes Bearer JWTs from web access logs and verifies their HMAC-SHA256 signature against the literal key 'random'. A successful verification is a smoking-gun forged token from the public CVE-2026-48031 secret. This is the highest-confidence detection but requires a custom enrichment step in the SIEM ingestion pipeline. Rationale: Implements the article's exact PoC inversely — the attacker uses 'random' as the HMAC key to sign; we use it to verify. Any token that verifies with key='random' is, by definition, a forged token because patched versions log.Fatal on that secret. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentester actively exploiting the CVE during an authorised engagement
  • Pre-prod environment that still ships the unpatched dev.env intentionally for testing
  • Bug-bounty researcher submitting a PoC against the production endpoint
  • An unrelated service that coincidentally also uses HS256 with the (weak) key 'random' for a different purpose
  • Token-replay testing tools (e.g. Burp JWT extension) being run by red team
Suppression filter
and SourceIP !in (KnownPenTesterIPs) and not (Environment == "staging" and ServiceName startswith "goose-base-test-")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the affected endpoint is running github.com/dhax/go-base. Decode the JWT 'sub' and 'roles' claims and check whether they correspond to a real user or a fabricated identity. Any 'roles' containing 'admin' is automatic priority-1. 2) Contain: rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to `openssl rand -base64 32`, redeploy the service to invalidate all outstanding tokens, force-logout all users, then patch the dhax/go-base dependency past commit cc82b9740fa6. Block the source IP at the WAF. 3) Hunt: pull every request from the offending IP over 30d; cross-correlate with DB audit logs for /api/v1/admin/users access, profile reads (/api/v1/me), and any state-mutating POST/PUT/DELETE. Identify what was touched and prepare a breach-notification scope.
// Requires custom Authorization-header capture into AdditionalFields on DeviceNetworkEvents.
// Decoded JWT verification is performed at ingest; this query surfaces records flagged JWTForged=true.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend Forged = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).JWTForgedWithKnownWeakSecret)
| where Forged == "true"
| extend JWTSubject = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).JWTSubject)
| extend JWTRoles = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).JWTRoles)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, JWTSubject, JWTRoles, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires a Logstash / Logic App enrichment that decodes Bearer JWTs and stamps a custom field 'JWTForgedWithKnownWeakSecret'=true when HMAC-SHA256 verifies against 'random'.
let Forged = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | extend Forged = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalExtensions).JWTForgedWithKnownWeakSecret)
    | where Forged == "true"
    | extend JWTSubject = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalExtensions).JWTSubject)
    | extend JWTRoles = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalExtensions).JWTRoles)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, SourceIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, JWTSubject, JWTRoles, RequestClientApplication;
Forged
| order by TimeGenerated desc
@jwt.forged_with_known_weak_secret:true OR @jwt.signing_key:random
# log group: /aws/applicationelb/access-logs  (ALB access logs — adjust per ELB; requires custom Lambda enricher that stamps jwt_forged=true)
fields @timestamp, request_url, client_ip, jwt_sub, jwt_roles, jwt_forged
| filter jwt_forged = "true"
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
WEB

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
