Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — web server spawning shell interpreter from terminal handler RCE AIInstallation High
Detects PHP-FPM / Apache / Nginx (or php-cgi) processes spawning sh/bash/dash under web service account context (www-data, apache, nginx). This is the post-exploitation footprint of the unsanitized 'dir' POST parameter in pheditor.php executing arbitrary OS commands via shell_exec(). Rationale: Article states 'achieving full Remote Code Execution with web server privileges' and PoC shows shell_exec() reaching sh via the cd-prefix injection from 'dir'. Pivot is the parent/child pair (PHP→sh) under web account — the exact runtime footprint of the exploit. Cross-checked NVD CVE-2026-48030 advisory and CWE-78 OS command injection canonical patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate site-management cron jobs run as www-data invoking shell helpers (e.g. WordPress wp-cron shelling out to mysqldump)
  • Composer install / npm postinstall scripts run under web user during deploy spawning bash to compile assets
  • Health-check scripts (Sensu, Datadog Agent) running as www-data executing /bin/sh probes
  • Legitimate Pheditor terminal commands the admin actually typed (ls, ps) reaching the same code path
  • Container init scripts in PHP base images where entrypoint is php-fpm and CMD launches bash
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/local/bin/wp","composer.phar","datadog-agent","sensu-client","newrelic-daemon") and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/")))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full ProcessCommandLine and ParentProcessCommandLine; look for 'pheditor.php' / 'action=terminal' in the parent chain and the article's IoC strings (cd <path>; curl, echo '<?php', /var/www/html/shell.php). Cross-reference web access logs for the same source IP hitting POST /pheditor.php within the prior 60s. 2) Contain — isolate the host via MDE Live Response or quarantine SG; revoke any pheditor admin credentials and rotate web-app session secret; block outbound from the web user to the attacker C2 IP. 3) Hunt — search DeviceFileEvents for .php writes under /var/www by web user (companion UC), DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound curl/wget egress, and AsepValueUpdate / crontab edits for persistence; pivot on the source IP across all internet-facing pheditor instances.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","php7.4","php8.0","php8.1","php8.2")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/","; curl","|sh","| sh","|bash","| bash","cd /var/www","cd /tmp","nc -e","bash -i")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/","|sh","| sh","|bash","| bash","cd /var/www","cd /tmp","nc -e","bash -i")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — shell metacharacters in 'dir' POST parameter to pheditor.php AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php with action=terminal where the 'dir' parameter (or surrounding body) carries shell metacharacters that bypass the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Web access / WAF / reverse-proxy telemetry catches the exploit at the network ingress before the PHP process spawns the shell. Rationale: Article's PoC Step 4 sends dir=/tmp; curl -s https://ifconfig.me # — the semicolon, pipe, backtick, $(, newline and >> set is the canonical OS-command-injection metachar list. POST to pheditor.php + action=terminal scope to the vulnerable endpoint, eliminating noise from GET-based feature use. WAF/proxy logs see the inbound request before PHP even spawns shell_exec. Validated against the GHSA advisory body and the CWE-78 / OWASP command-injection metachar catalogue. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Command_Injection • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin pasting a directory path containing a space-then-semicolon (rare; benign)
  • Pen-test or vulnerability-scanner traffic (Nessus, Qualys, Burp scanner) probing the endpoint
  • Browser auto-filled previous-session 'dir' values containing $ or backtick if used inside the path
  • Encoded-but-benign characters introduced by client-side JS that URL-encodes the path twice
  • Internal QA / staging environments where developers test terminal commands intentionally
Suppression filter
| where not (csUserAgent has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","InternalSecScan") and cIP startswith "10.")
Response runbook
1) Triage — extract the source IP, the exact decoded 'dir' payload, and whether the response was 200 vs blocked; pivot on the same SrcIp across all pheditor.php hits in the last 24h to spot enumeration. 2) Contain — block source IP at WAF / edge; rotate the pheditor admin password (article shows default 'admin'); if Pheditor 2.0.1–2.0.3, immediately disable the terminal permission in config or take pheditor.php offline pending patch. 3) Hunt — correlate to the companion UC for php→sh spawning on the same host within ±60s, search DeviceFileEvents for new .php files under /var/www, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to attacker IPs (ifconfig.me, attacker-controlled curl targets).
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem endswith "pheditor.php"
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriQuery has_any ("%3B","%7C","%26%26","%24%28","%60","%0A")
        or csUriStem has_any (";","|","&&","$(","`")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, ClientIP=cIP, csUserAgent, csUserName, scStatus),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Message has_any ("action=terminal","dir=")
    | where Message has_any (";","|","&&","$(","`","%3B","%7C","%26%26","%24%28","%60","%0A")
        or RequestContext has_any (";","|","&&","$(","`")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestMethod, RequestURL, ClientIP=SourceIP, RequestClientApplication, Message, RequestContext),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has "pheditor.php"
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has_any ("action=terminal","%3B","%7C","%26%26","%24%28","%60")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, HttpMethod, Url, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — webshell drop: PHP / web account writing .php to webroot AIInstallation High
Detects file-creation events where a web service process (php-fpm, apache2, nginx, php-cgi) or its child shell writes a .php file into /var/www, /srv/www or /usr/share/nginx/html under the web service account. Article PoC Step 5 drops `<?php system($_GET['c']);?>` to /var/www/html/shell.php — this catches the persistence stage of the exploit. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5: `echo '<?php system($_GET["c"]);?>' > /var/www/html/shell.php` — the canonical PHP webshell drop. Process-writes-PHP-into-webroot-as-web-user is the cleanest pivot because legit deploys are done by root / deploy-bot, NOT by www-data; this combination is high-fidelity for any PHP-RCE post-exploit, not just Pheditor. Cross-referenced against MITRE T1505.003 webshell technique and ATT&CK Linux execution case studies. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CMS auto-update (WordPress core/plugin updates) running as www-data writing .php into webroot
  • Composer install run as www-data during in-place deploy populating vendor/*.php
  • File-upload features in legitimate apps that store user-supplied .php (rare — usually blocked, but some plugins permit)
  • Theme/plugin install workflows in dev / staging environments
  • Cache-generation systems that materialise .php views (Symfony cache:warmup, Smarty compiled templates) into webroot-adjacent paths
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("wp-cron.php","composer.phar","symfony") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("upgrade","cache:warmup","composer install"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull SHA256 + first 512 bytes of the dropped file; webshell signatures like `<?php system($_GET`, `eval($_POST`, `passthru($_REQUEST`, `assert(stripslashes(`, base64-only bodies are conclusive. Identify the parent shell command and tie it back to the pheditor.php POST via the companion UCs. 2) Contain — quarantine / delete the file via MDE Live Response (capture a copy for IR first), isolate the host, rotate web-user-readable secrets (DB credentials in .env / wp-config.php), and remove pheditor.php from the webroot until patched. 3) Hunt — fingerprint the webshell hash across all hosts via DeviceFileEvents, search DeviceNetworkEvents for GET requests hitting the dropped filename (shell.php?c=...), and check for additional persistence (cron, systemd timers, .ssh/authorized_keys, /etc/ld.so.preload).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","sh","bash","dash")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/nginx/html/","/srv/http/")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","sh","bash","dash")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/nginx/html/","/srv/http/")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php" or TargetFileName endswith ".phtml" or TargetFileName endswith ".phar"
   or TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar")
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — vulnerable Pheditor 2.0.1–2.0.3 asset inventory exposure AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts running pheditor/pheditor in the affected version range (>=2.0.1, <=2.0.3) and flags internet-facing instances for priority patching. Combines TVM vulnerability data with DeviceInfo internet-facing tag so SOC can prioritise external exposure first. Rationale: GHSA states affected range composer:pheditor/pheditor >=2.0.1, <=2.0.3. Pairing TVM software inventory + CVE lookup with DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing is the textbook 'patch the exposed assets first' pivot and stops the exploit before any of the runtime UCs even fire. Cross-checked against the GitHub advisory packages section and the composer/packagist package listing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://packagist.org/packages/pheditor/pheditor
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM not seeing the package because pheditor was installed via composer without registering in OS package manager (false negative more than positive)
  • Test/lab hosts running Pheditor intentionally for security research — flagged but not actionable
  • Mirror / replica instances where the canary version string was patched but the binary itself wasn't
  • Vendor-shipped appliances bundling pheditor as a sub-component without exposing version string
  • CMDB stale records pointing at decommissioned hosts that no longer run pheditor
Response runbook
1) Triage — for each hit, confirm pheditor is actually running (curl -I http://host/pheditor.php) and capture the version banner from the login page; record whether terminal permission is enabled (article notes default-on). 2) Contain — for internet-facing hits, take the endpoint offline behind WAF deny or remove the vhost until patched; rotate the pheditor admin password (article PoC used 'admin'); enforce IP allow-listing on the management endpoint. 3) Hunt — for every host on this list, retro-search the companion UCs (POST to pheditor.php with metachars, php→sh spawn, .php writes to webroot) over the last 90 days to determine if exploitation already happened pre-patch.
let Vuln = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

let Inv = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

let Surface = DeviceInfo
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, MachineGroup, OSPlatform) by DeviceId, DeviceName;
union Vuln, Inv
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
| join kind=leftouter Surface on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, MachineGroup

Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-06-09 10 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 research examines attack scenarios targeting cloud logging services. Learn how to defend against log manipulation and defense evasion. The post Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1190 T1566
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] AWS CloudTrail UpdateTrail config tampering (S3 destination swap or validation disabled)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS CloudTrail trail disabled or deleted (StopLogging / DeleteTrail) · [LLM] AWS CloudTrail S3 destination bucket emptied or deleted · [LLM] GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted · [LLM] AWS CloudWatch Logs group deleted or retention shortened to 1 day · [LLM] AWS CloudTrail log file integrity validation disabled (EnableLogFileValidation=false)
AWS CloudTrail trail disabled or deleted (StopLogging / DeleteTrail) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects an IAM principal invoking cloudtrail:StopLogging or cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, which the article describes as Technique 1 — the most direct way to blind defenders by suspending log delivery to the configured S3 bucket. High-confidence signal: legitimate admin teardowns are rare and usually scheduled. Rationale: Article Technique 1 names the exact APIs (cloudtrail:StopLogging) and impact (no further logs written to S3). Cross-checked AWS CloudTrail API docs and MITRE T1562.008 page — both confirm StopLogging/DeleteTrail as defender-blinding actions. errorCode-absent filter ensures we only alert on successful evasion, not denied attempts (which themselves indicate recon and could be a separate hunt). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/ • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_StopLogging.html
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled trail decommission during multi-account consolidation (Control Tower / Organizations migrations)
  • Terraform/CloudFormation stack deletions that own the trail being recreated immediately after
  • IaC drift remediation where a duplicate trail is being cleaned up
  • Disaster-recovery testing in a sandbox account
  • Cost-cutting exercise replacing per-region trails with an org-wide trail
Suppression filter
| where userIdentity.userName !startswith "terraform-" and UserAgent !has "aws-internal"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the userIdentity.arn — is this a human IAM user, a CI/CD role (e.g. Terraform/Atlantis), or an AssumedRole from a workstation? Pull the 24h activity window for that principal in CloudTrail and check for change-control ticket references in userAgent. Step 2 (contain): If unauthorized, re-create the trail immediately and revoke the principal's cloudtrail:* permissions via SCP or inline deny; rotate any active session via sts:RevokeSession. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on sourceIPAddress for any iam:CreateAccessKey, iam:AttachUserPolicy, or s3:DeleteBucket activity within ±1h — StopLogging is almost always the prelude to a larger action the attacker doesn't want logged.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("StopLogging", "DeleteTrail")
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).requestParameters.name)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, ActionType, TrailName, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName in ("StopLogging", "DeleteTrail")
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityType, SourceIpAddress, AWSRegion, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AWS CloudTrail Logging Stopped or Trail Deleted
id: 3c1f9a6e-2e4d-4f87-9c84-8a73e0b1a9c1
description: Detects cloudtrail:StopLogging or cloudtrail:DeleteTrail API calls used to blind defenders, as described in Unit 42 'Blinding the Watchmen'.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cloud-logging-defense-evasion/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  - attack.t1562.008
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: cloudtrail.amazonaws.com
    eventName:
      - StopLogging
      - DeleteTrail
  filter_failed:
    errorCode: '*'
  condition: selection and not filter_failed
level: high

# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress, awsRegion, requestParameters.name
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"

| limit 100
CLOUD
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" (eventName="StopLogging" OR eventName="DeleteTrail") NOT errorCode="*" | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress, awsRegion, eventName, requestParameters.name | where count >= 1
AWS CloudTrail S3 destination bucket emptied or deleted AIActions on Objectives High
Detects s3:DeleteBucket (and the preceding bulk s3:DeleteObject) against a bucket that is the configured CloudTrail destination — Technique 2 in the article. CloudTrail's UI surfaces a 'bucket not found' indicator a few minutes after, but by then forensic archive is gone. Rationale: Article Figure 2 caption explicitly shows the CloudTrail console indicator after s3:DeleteBucket; Technique 2 names the exact API combination (s3:DeleteBucket + s3:DeleteObject). The Sentinel join enriches with which trail the bucket served — an analyst doesn't have to look it up at 3am. Cross-checked the AWS S3 API reference and MITRE T1562.008. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/ • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteBucket.html
ATT&CKT1562.008 T1070.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate trail-bucket migration during account consolidation
  • Terraform destroy on a sandbox account that owned its own trail
  • Lifecycle-policy-driven bucket cleanup when archive moves to Glacier in a different bucket
  • DR tabletop where the trail is being re-pointed at a new bucket
  • Cost cleanup of an abandoned dev trail
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "terraform" and UserAgent !has "cloudformation"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the deleted bucket name against your CloudTrail trail inventory (CreateTrail/UpdateTrail history) — only escalate if it was actively serving a production trail. Pull the past 7 days of userIdentity activity. Step 2 (contain): Revoke the principal's s3:Delete* and cloudtrail:* permissions via SCP; if logs landed in a CloudWatch Logs subscription, switch incident analysis there until S3 is restored from versioning or replicated archive. Step 3 (hunt): Look for s3:PutBucketVersioning Status=Suspended in the 24h preceding the delete (attackers must disable versioning first to prevent recovery), and any iam:CreateAccessKey by the same principal — they often pre-stage egress credentials before destroying logs.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType == "DeleteBucket"
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).requestParameters.bucketName)
| where isnotempty(BucketName)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, BucketName, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let TrailBuckets = AWSCloudTrail
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventName in ("CreateTrail", "UpdateTrail")
    | extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).s3BucketName)
    | where isnotempty(BucketName)
    | summarize TrailNames = make_set(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)) by BucketName;
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "s3.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName == "DeleteBucket"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName)
| join kind=inner TrailBuckets on BucketName
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, BucketName, TrailNames, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:DeleteBucket @evt.outcome:success @eventSource:s3.amazonaws.com
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.bucketName
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "DeleteBucket"
| filter not isPresent(errorCode)
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
CLOUD
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="s3.amazonaws.com" eventName="DeleteBucket" NOT errorCode="*" | rename requestParameters.bucketName as bucketName | join type=left bucketName [ search index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" eventName IN ("CreateTrail","UpdateTrail","GetTrail") | rename requestParameters.s3BucketName as bucketName | stats values(requestParameters.name) as trailName by bucketName ] | where isnotnull(trailName) | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, bucketName, trailName
AWS CloudTrail UpdateTrail config tampering (S3 destination swap or validation disabled) AICommand & Control High
Detects cloudtrail:UpdateTrail calls that re-point a trail's S3BucketName to an attacker-controlled bucket, disable log file integrity validation (EnableLogFileValidation=false), or replace event selectors to exclude write events. Captures the Continuous Visibility scenario from the article — quietly redirecting the org's logs into the adversary's own account. Rationale: Article's 'Continuous Visibility' section describes attackers transferring logs to their own accounts — a destination swap via UpdateTrail is the cleanest implementation; reviewer feedback #5 calls out validation-disable specifically. Both conditions are rare in legitimate ops because trails are usually IaC-managed. Cross-checked AWS UpdateTrail API doc. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateTrail.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/
ATT&CKT1562.008 T1530
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/CloudFormation re-applying with a renamed S3 bucket
  • Security team migrating to a centralized log archive account
  • Compliance team enabling log validation (true) — not malicious; ensure detection filters on false
  • One-time SRE-driven KMS-encryption rollout that re-emits UpdateTrail with the same bucket
  • Org-wide trail consolidation by AWS Control Tower
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "cloudformation.amazonaws.com" and UserAgent !has "terraform"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Diff the new s3BucketName against the inventory of org-owned buckets — if it's a 12-digit account ID you don't own, escalate immediately. Check userAgent for IaC tooling fingerprints. Step 2 (contain): Revert the trail config to the known-good bucket, revoke the principal's cloudtrail:UpdateTrail via SCP, and S3-block-public-access on the rogue destination if it's reachable. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the source account/principal for sts:AssumeRole chains in the prior 24h, and search for the same modus operandi on other trails or on Config recorders (PutDeliveryChannel) — the same playbook applies cross-service.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType == "UpdateTrail"
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend TrailName = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.name)
| extend NewBucket = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.s3BucketName)
| extend LogValidation = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation)
| where isnotempty(NewBucket) or LogValidation == "false"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, TrailName, NewBucket, LogValidation, IPAddress, UserAgent, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName == "UpdateTrail"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend Req = parse_json(RequestParameters)
| extend TrailName = tostring(Req.name)
| extend NewBucket = tostring(Req.s3BucketName)
| extend LogValidation = tostring(Req.enableLogFileValidation)
| where isnotempty(NewBucket) or LogValidation == "false"
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, TrailName, NewBucket, LogValidation, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:UpdateTrail @evt.outcome:success (@requestParameters.s3BucketName:* OR @requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation:false)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.name, requestParameters.s3BucketName, requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "UpdateTrail"
| filter not isPresent(errorCode)
| filter isPresent(requestParameters.s3BucketName) or requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation = "false"
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
CLOUD
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" eventName="UpdateTrail" NOT errorCode="*" | rename requestParameters.name as trailName, requestParameters.s3BucketName as newBucket, requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation as logValidation | eval evasion=case(logValidation=="false","validation_disabled", isnotnull(newBucket),"destination_swapped", 1==1,"other") | where evasion!="other" | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, values(evasion) as evasionType, count by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, trailName, newBucket, logValidation
GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted AIActions on Objectives High
Detects google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink with disabled=true or DeleteSink against a routing sink — Technique 1 / 2 equivalents for GCP described in the article. Sink disable is the exact control the article's Figure 1 console message confirms. Rationale: Article explicitly names logging.sinks.update with disabled=true (Figure 1) and logging.buckets.delete (Technique 2 for GCP); MITRE T1562.008 page confirms GCP sink disable as a sub-technique example. Sentinel KQL left empty because Sentinel's canonical schema in this tenant does not include a validated GCP Cloud Audit table — operators on AWSCloudTrail-only tenants should consume via Datadog gcp.audit or native GCP Security Command Center. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/ • https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform run that re-creates a sink (delete + create pair)
  • Project decommission where parent project removes child-project sinks
  • Cost-cutting exercise disabling verbose sinks before quarterly review
  • Folder-level sink supersedes a project-level sink and the redundant one is removed
  • DR drill where logging is being re-pointed to a different log bucket
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Look up the sink name and project; confirm whether it was the org's _Default sink (which captures all admin activity) or a custom-purpose sink. Pull the principalEmail's 24h GCP activity. Step 2 (contain): Recreate the sink from IaC/Terraform state; revoke the principal's roles/logging.configWriter and roles/logging.admin via gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding. Step 3 (hunt): Search for iam.serviceAccountKeys.create or setIamPolicy by the same principal in the prior 24h — sink disable usually precedes credential theft or resource exfil the attacker doesn't want exported to Splunk/Chronicle.
title: GCP Cloud Logging Sink Disabled or Deleted
id: 9e2d6b34-1f5c-4d2a-8e74-3b89c1e5a4f2
description: Detects routing-sink disable or deletion in GCP Cloud Logging — Technique 1/2 from Unit 42 'Blinding the Watchmen'.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cloud-logging-defense-evasion/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.008
logsource:
  product: gcp
  service: gcp.audit
detection:
  selection_delete:
    methodName: 'google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink'
  selection_update_disabled:
    methodName: 'google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink'
    request.sink.disabled: true
  condition: selection_delete or selection_update_disabled
level: high
source:gcp.audit (@protoPayload.methodName:google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink OR (@protoPayload.methodName:google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink AND @protoPayload.request.sink.disabled:true))
CLOUD
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" (protoPayload.methodName="google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink" OR (protoPayload.methodName="google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink" AND protoPayload.request.sink.disabled=true)) | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp, protoPayload.methodName, protoPayload.resourceName, resource.labels.project_id
AWS CloudWatch Logs group deleted or retention shortened to 1 day AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects logs:DeleteLogGroup or logs:PutRetentionPolicy that drops retention to 1 day on a CloudWatch Logs group — covers the article's Technique 2 (delete log storage destination) for the CloudWatch Logs delivery path mentioned as an alternative to S3, and reviewer feedback #3. Rationale: Article's Background section names CloudWatch Logs explicitly as an alternative CloudTrail destination, and reviewer feedback #3 calls out DeleteLogGroup/PutRetentionPolicy as the equivalent of bucket destruction. Retention=1 is the lowest the API allows and is functionally equivalent to deletion within the attack window. Cross-checked AWS CloudWatch Logs API reference. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteLogGroup.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/
ATT&CKT1562.008 T1070.007
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev/test pipeline shortening retention to control costs in ephemeral accounts
  • Lambda function being torn down with its log group
  • Terraform destroy on a stack that owns its own log group
  • Lifecycle automation moving archives to S3 with reduced CloudWatch retention
  • Org-level retention policy reducing per-group retention as part of cost optimization
Suppression filter
| where LogGroup startswith "/aws/cloudtrail" or LogGroup startswith "/aws/guardduty" or LogGroup startswith "/aws/vpc/flowlogs" or LogGroup contains "audit"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Check whether the log group is on the inventory of security-relevant groups (/aws/cloudtrail, /aws/guardduty, /aws/vpc/flowlogs, audit-Lambdas). Anything outside that list is likely benign noise. Step 2 (contain): If security-relevant, restore retention via PutRetentionPolicy and revoke logs:Delete*/logs:PutRetentionPolicy from the principal via SCP. Pull any subscription filters that may have shipped logs to a sibling SIEM — those may still hold a copy. Step 3 (hunt): Look for parallel s3:DeleteBucket / cloudtrail:StopLogging / config:DeleteDeliveryChannel by the same principal in ±1h — multi-surface log destruction is the unmistakable pre-action pattern.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("DeleteLogGroup", "PutRetentionPolicy")
| extend Req = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).requestParameters
| extend LogGroup = tostring(Req.logGroupName)
| extend RetentionDays = toint(Req.retentionInDays)
| where ActionType == "DeleteLogGroup" or (ActionType == "PutRetentionPolicy" and RetentionDays <= 1)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, ActionType, LogGroup, RetentionDays, IPAddress, UserAgent, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "logs.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName in ("DeleteLogGroup", "PutRetentionPolicy")
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend Req = parse_json(RequestParameters)
| extend LogGroup = tostring(Req.logGroupName)
| extend RetentionDays = toint(Req.retentionInDays)
| where EventName == "DeleteLogGroup" or (EventName == "PutRetentionPolicy" and RetentionDays <= 1)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, LogGroup, RetentionDays, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:cloudtrail @evt.outcome:success ((@evt.name:DeleteLogGroup) OR (@evt.name:PutRetentionPolicy AND @requestParameters.retentionInDays:<=1))
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.logGroupName, requestParameters.retentionInDays
| filter eventSource = "logs.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName in ["DeleteLogGroup", "PutRetentionPolicy"]
| filter not isPresent(errorCode)
| filter eventName = "DeleteLogGroup" or requestParameters.retentionInDays <= 1
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
CLOUD
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="logs.amazonaws.com" (eventName="DeleteLogGroup" OR (eventName="PutRetentionPolicy" AND requestParameters.retentionInDays<=1)) NOT errorCode="*" | rename requestParameters.logGroupName as logGroup, requestParameters.retentionInDays as retentionDays | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, values(eventName) as actions, values(retentionDays) as retentionDays, count by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, logGroup
AWS CloudTrail log file integrity validation disabled (EnableLogFileValidation=false) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects cloudtrail:UpdateTrail or cloudtrail:CreateTrail with EnableLogFileValidation set to false — the article's title 'Blinding the Watchmen' captures the intent and reviewer feedback #5 calls this out specifically. Without digest files, log tampering becomes undetectable. Rationale: Reviewer feedback #5 explicitly grounds this: disabling EnableLogFileValidation removes the SHA-256 digest chain that proves logs were not tampered with, precisely the 'Blinding the Watchmen' theme. AWS CIS Benchmark 2.2 and Security Hub PCI.CloudTrail.1 also require this to be true — a legitimate flip to false should be an exception, not the norm. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-log-file-validation-intro.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IaC drift where the Terraform template was authored before validation was required
  • New sandbox trail created without validation enabled
  • Cost-driven flip during a digest-storage cleanup exercise
  • Migration from CloudTrail Lake (which doesn't use digest files) and someone forgot to re-enable on the file trail
  • One-time compliance evidence-gathering exercise that briefly toggles validation off
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "terraform" and UserAgent !has "cloudformation"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the trail history (DescribeTrails) and confirm validation was previously enabled — a fresh CreateTrail with validation off is lower-severity than a flip on a long-lived prod trail. Identify the IAM principal and userAgent. Step 2 (contain): Re-enable via cloudtrail:UpdateTrail EnableLogFileValidation=true and revoke cloudtrail:Update*/Create* from the principal via SCP if unauthorized. Step 3 (hunt): Search S3 PutObject events against the trail bucket for the 24h window after validation was disabled — any objects placed by a principal other than cloudtrail.amazonaws.com indicate log injection (Technique 5: Log poisoning).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("UpdateTrail", "CreateTrail")
| extend Req = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).requestParameters
| extend TrailName = tostring(Req.name)
| extend LogValidation = tostring(Req.enableLogFileValidation)
| where LogValidation == "false"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, ActionType, TrailName, LogValidation, IPAddress, UserAgent, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName in ("UpdateTrail", "CreateTrail")
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend Req = parse_json(RequestParameters)
| extend TrailName = tostring(Req.name)
| extend LogValidation = tostring(Req.enableLogFileValidation)
| where LogValidation == "false"
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityType, SourceIpAddress, AWSRegion, TrailName, LogValidation, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AWS CloudTrail Log File Validation Disabled
id: b71c4e5d-3a82-49f8-bd1e-7e2f93a8c5b3
description: Detects UpdateTrail/CreateTrail setting EnableLogFileValidation=false, removing the cryptographic digest that proves logs were not tampered with.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cloud-logging-defense-evasion/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1562.008
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: cloudtrail.amazonaws.com
    eventName:
      - UpdateTrail
      - CreateTrail
    requestParameters.logFileValidationEnabled: false
  condition: selection
level: high
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(UpdateTrail OR CreateTrail) @evt.outcome:success @requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation:false
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.name, requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName in ["UpdateTrail", "CreateTrail"]
| filter not isPresent(errorCode)
| filter requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation = "false" or requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation = false
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
CLOUD
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" (eventName="UpdateTrail" OR eventName="CreateTrail") requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation=false NOT errorCode="*" | rename requestParameters.name as trailName | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress, awsRegion, trailName, eventName
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

        ParentImage|endswith:

            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'

            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'

            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
